digest.component_or_area: CI linting and store write enforcement
propositions: Multiple production bugs (3435, 3a33, 4dd2, 4c6c) resulted from store write paths that bypassed canonical write seams by using raw git add/commit/rm commands outside sanctioned APIs.

A deterministic two-layer lint (Python AST layer and workflow/shell layer) must flag raw git mutation verbs (add/commit/rm/mv/reset/update-ref/checkout/clean) unless marked with an inline '# raw-git-ok: <reason>' marker carrying mandatory justification.

The lint must distinguish between two legitimate write seams (store layer via gitutil/event_append/txn and reconciler layer via git_adapter/_ref_lock) and illegitimate bypasses by tracking mutation verbs through local intra-function variable assignment and splat expansion, failing closed on opaque argv.

Workflow and shell scripts are flagged for git mutations only when the same step/block establishes tracker context via cd into .tickets-tracker, git -C <tracker-path>, or working-directory targeting the tracker directory.

All historical bypass sites and seam-internal writes must be inventoried and remediated or marked during a report-mode bootstrap before enforcement is enabled, with the authoritative inventory produced by the lint itself rather than prose enumeration.
